funeral-costs-new-mexico.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in New Mexico

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in New Mexico must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. State oversight sits with the New Mexico Board of Funeral Services in the Regulation and Licensing Department, which licenses and regulates funeral directors, funeral homes and crematoriums; its stated first duty is to protect the public in the handling and care of the dead.
The Funeral Consumers Alliance does not list New Mexico

The Funeral Consumers Alliance does not list New Mexico among the nine states that require a funeral director for parts of after-death care, so a New Mexico family may arrange much of a funeral itself. The New Mexico death certificate and disposition permit still have to be filed. Certified copies come from the Bureau of Vital Records and Health Statistics in Santa Fe, which lists a death certificate ordered through VitalChek at $21.00 with regular mail delivery or $39.50 with next-day air.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in South Dakota

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in South Dakota must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. The South Dakota Board of Funeral Service, listed with the Department of Health's licensing boards, takes consumer complaints, inspects funeral homes and crematories, and registers funeral service trainees; its office is in Spearfish (605-642-1600). It is not the South Dakota Funeral Association, which is a trade group that promotes the profession.
The Funeral Consumers Alliance does not list South Dakota

The Funeral Consumers Alliance does not list South Dakota among the nine states that require a funeral director for parts of after-death care, so a South Dakota family may arrange much of a funeral itself. The South Dakota death certificate and disposition permit still have to be filed. Certified copies are issued by Vital Records at the South Dakota Department of Health, 221 West Capitol Avenue in Pierre (605-773-4961), which takes orders in person, by mail, by phone or online.
funeral-costs-wyoming.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Wyoming

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Wyoming must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. Licensing is handled by the Wyoming State Board of Funeral Service Practitioners, which began in 1915 as the Board of Embalming. When the Legislature renamed it in 2014, it also dropped the separate funeral director license, so everyone licensed to practice funeral service in Wyoming is now a funeral service practitioner.
If you believe a funeral home in Wyoming

If you believe a funeral home in Wyoming has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. To report a Wyoming funeral home, use the board's public complaint process. Its office in the Emerson Building no longer takes walk-ins, so call 307-777-5403 to set up a visit.
funeral-costs-arizona.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Arizona

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Arizona must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. In Arizona, funeral services licensing is run by the Arizona Department of Health Services, whose funeral services pages also carry consumer guides and the annual trust reports.
If you believe a funeral home in Arizona

If you believe a funeral home in Arizona has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. The Arizona Department of Health Services also takes complaints about funeral homes through its online complaint form.
funeral-costs-georgia.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Georgia

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Georgia must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. The Georgia State Board of Funeral Service, part of the Secretary of State's Professional Licensing Boards Division, licenses funeral directors, embalmers, funeral establishments and crematories, and an establishment whose owner is not a funeral director must name a licensed funeral director in full and continuous charge.
If you believe a funeral home in Georgia

If you believe a funeral home in Georgia has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. Complaints about a Georgia funeral home are filed in writing through the Secretary of State's online GOALS system, with the licensee's name and license number if you have them; Georgia law keeps complaints confidential (O.C.G.A. § 43-1-19).
funeral-costs-montana.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Montana

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Montana must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. The Montana Board of Funeral Service licenses morticians and mortician interns, mortuaries, crematory operators and technicians, crematories and for-profit cemeteries, and its members include a cemetery company representative and one member of the public.
If you believe a funeral home in Montana

If you believe a funeral home in Montana has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. Complaints against a Montana licensee go to the Department of Labor and Industry's complaint line, (406) 841-2362.
funeral-costs-kansas.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Kansas

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Kansas must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. State licensing belongs to the Kansas State Board of Mortuary Arts, whose stated mission is to make sure its licensees work in a way that gives the people of Kansas maximum protection of their health, safety and welfare.
If you believe a funeral home in Kansas

If you believe a funeral home in Kansas has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. Questions or complaints about a Kansas funeral home can go to the board at 700 SW Jackson Street, Suite 904, in Topeka (785-296-3980).
funeral-costs-kentucky.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Kentucky

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Kentucky must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. The Kentucky Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors is a small agency, with five board members and a staff of three in Louisville, that licenses individuals and funeral establishments. It also issues courtesy cards that let a funeral director licensed in Indiana, Ohio, Virginia or West Virginia carry a body into or out of Kentucky and conduct services and burials here.
If you believe a funeral home in Kentucky

If you believe a funeral home in Kentucky has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. To raise a problem with a Kentucky funeral home, contact the board at 502-426-4589 or KBEFD@ky.gov, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
funeral-costs-arkansas.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Arkansas

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Arkansas must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. In Arkansas, funeral homes answer to the State Board of Embalmers, Funeral Directors, Cemeteries, and Burial Services inside the Arkansas Insurance Department. Act 788 of 2017 created it by abolishing the old embalmers board, the Burial Association Board and the Arkansas Cemetery Board.
If you believe a funeral home in Arkansas

If you believe a funeral home in Arkansas has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. The department's Funeral Services Division also handles prepaid funeral benefits (501-371-2683) and perpetual care cemeteries (501-371-2646), so a question about a preneed contract or a cemetery can go to the same place.
funeral-costs-maine.html: Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Maine

Know Your Rights Under the FTC Funeral Rule Every funeral home in Maine must comply with the Federal Trade Commission's Funeral Rule, which protects consumers nationwide. The Maine Board of Funeral Service, part of the Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation, licenses funeral service practitioners and funeral homes, and under 32 M.R.S. § 1451 its inspections can include the financial records behind prearranged funeral plans.
If you believe a funeral home in Maine

If you believe a funeral home in Maine has violated these rights, you can file a complaint with the FTC at ftc.gov or contact the Funeral Consumers Alliance for guidance. Board staff take questions and complaints at (207) 624-8624; the board asks the public not to contact board members directly.
cremation-costs-idaho.html: Get the Idaho provider's General Price List

Under Idaho Code § 54-1139, a person who funds a prearranged funeral plan can put cremation instructions in it and sign the cremation authorization form ahead of time. Anything the plan does not clearly cover falls back to the next-of-kin order in § 54-1142, and simply owning a burial plot does not count as a prearranged plan.
In short, Idaho has no fixed minimum waiting period

Idaho sets no minimum waiting period, but the paperwork has its own steps. Under Idaho Code § 39-268, the mortician who first takes charge of the body reports to the district registrar within 24 hours, and whoever signs the death certificate authorizes final disposition. For a cremation, the coroner must also give an additional authorization, and the crematory still needs a signed authorization from the next of kin or designated agent. For the funeral-director question and who takes complaints, see the cremation rules and help section lower on this page.
cremation-costs-missouri.html: Get the Missouri provider's General Price List

Missouri's right-of-sepulcher law, RSMo § 194.119, sets who may authorize a cremation: first an attorney in fact given that right in a durable power of attorney, then the person a service member who died on active duty named on DD Form 93, then the spouse, a child, a parent, a sibling and the next nearest relative. After them come a friend who agrees to pay and, last, the county coroner or medical examiner.
In short, Missouri has no fixed minimum waiting period

Missouri sets no fixed minimum waiting period, but it does set out who may decide. Under RSMo § 194.119, anyone who wants to make the arrangements must first notify a person with a higher claim, and that person waives the right by not objecting within 48 hours of being notified in person or by written notice with delivery confirmation. The crematory still needs the death certificate, a cremation permit and the signed authorization. For the funeral-director question and who takes complaints, see the cremation rules and help section lower on this page.
cremation-costs-montana.html: Get the Montana provider's General Price List

Montana's priority list in MCA 37-19-904 starts with the person a service member named on Defense Department Form 93, then anyone the decedent designated in a notarized affidavit, then the spouse. After that the decision passes to a majority of the surviving children, then the parents, then a majority of the siblings; fewer than half of the children may act only after reasonable efforts to notify the rest and with no known opposition from a majority.
burial-costs-arkansas.html: Funeral homes handling burials in Arkansas are licensed by the Arkansas Insurance Department, Funeral Services Division (501-682-0574).

Funeral homes handling burials in Arkansas are licensed by the Arkansas Insurance Department, Funeral Services Division (501-682-0574). The same division also oversees perpetual care cemeteries (501-371-2646) and prepaid funeral benefits (501-371-2683), because Act 788 of 2017 folded the old Arkansas Cemetery Board and the embalmers board into one board inside the Insurance Department.
burial-costs-kentucky.html: Funeral homes handling burials in Kentucky are licensed by the Kentucky Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors (502-426-4589).

Funeral homes handling burials in Kentucky are licensed by the Kentucky Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors (502-426-4589). Cemeteries answer to a different office: under KRS 367.946, every Kentucky cemetery company and anyone selling preneed cemetery merchandise must register with the Attorney General, and KRS 367.954 requires 40% of the payments for merchandise not installed within six months to be held in trust, unless the seller posts a bond instead.
burial-costs-massachusetts.html: Funeral homes handling burials in Massachusetts are licensed by the Massachusetts Board of Embalming and Funeral Directing (617-701-8628).

Funeral homes handling burials in Massachusetts are licensed by the Massachusetts Board of Embalming and Funeral Directing (617-701-8628). That board does not regulate cemeteries, which in Massachusetts operate separately from funeral homes and may be municipal, private, corporate or religious. The state's funeral consumer fact sheet tells families with a cemetery problem to start with the cemetery's management and the local board of health where the cemetery is located.
burial-costs-delaware.html: Funeral homes handling burials in Delaware are licensed by the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation (302-744-4500).

Funeral homes handling burials in Delaware are licensed by the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation (302-744-4500). The Delaware Cemetery Board in the Division of Public Health keeps a cemetery registration and runs the Distressed Cemetery Fund, but it has no enforcement power (29 Del. C. §§ 7901A and 7904A); it refers consumer complaints elsewhere, including to the Department of Justice's Consumer Protection Unit (800-220-5424).
burial-costs-louisiana.html: Funeral homes handling burials in Louisiana are licensed by the Louisiana State Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors (504-838-5109).

Funeral homes handling burials in Louisiana are licensed by the Louisiana State Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors (504-838-5109). Cemeteries have their own regulator: the Louisiana Cemetery Board, created by Act 417 of 1974, licenses cemetery authorities and cemetery sales organizations, audits perpetual care and merchandise trust funds, and mediates consumer complaints.
burial-costs-rhode-island.html: Northeastern burial costs in Rhode Island are pushed up by real estate

Rhode Island law protects the upkeep money built into a plot price. Under R.I. Gen. Laws § 23-18-8.1, perpetual care funds must be kept separate from a cemetery's other money, and at least 20% of the sale price of a lot, crypt or niche sold with perpetual care must go into that fund. Older municipal and religious cemeteries in Rhode Island were often set up on land donated or endowed long ago, and their pricing can still reflect that. A 15-minute longer drive to one of these can cut $1,760 or more off your cemetery bill.
funeral-costs-virginia.html: If a funeral home in Virginia refuses to show prices

If a funeral home in Virginia refuses to show prices or pressures you, the licensing body is the Virginia Board of Funeral Directors and Embalmers, reachable at 804-367-4479. The board has nine members, sits within the Department of Health Professions, and besides funeral directors and embalmers it also licenses crematories, surface transportation and removal services, and courtesy card holders.
funeral-costs-north-carolina.html: Funeral homes in North Carolina are licensed by

Funeral homes in North Carolina are licensed by the North Carolina Board of Funeral Service (919-733-9380). That office takes North Carolina complaints about pricing, misleading sales, or a home that will not hand over its price list. The board dates to 1901, when its first members were appointed by the State Board of Health; today the Governor and the General Assembly appoint them. Its meetings, usually held on the second Wednesday of the month at 1033 Wade Avenue in Raleigh, are open to the public and streamed live on YouTube.
funeral-costs-florida.html: The Florida Department of Financial Services licenses

The Florida Department of Financial Services licenses funeral directors and establishments in Florida; call 850-413-3039 to check a license or file a complaint. Within that department, the Division of Funeral, Cemetery, and Consumer Services inspects licensed establishments, facilities and cemetery grounds every year, and its licensing reaches beyond funeral directing and embalming to cremation, preneed sales, cemeteries and monument sales.
Individual prices in Florida still vary by provider
Individual prices in Florida still vary by provider, and the Florida Board of Funeral, Cemetery, and Consumer Services licenses Florida homes without setting their prices.
funeral-costs-indiana.html: The Indiana Professional Licensing Agency licenses

The Indiana Professional Licensing Agency licenses funeral directors and establishments in Indiana; call 317-234-3031 to check a license or file a complaint. The agency staffs the State Board of Funeral and Cemetery Service, which also oversees two consumer funds, the Preneed Consumer Protection Fund and the Consumer Protection Fund for Cemetery Maintenance.
funeral-costs-idaho.html: The Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses licenses

The Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses licenses funeral directors and establishments in Idaho; call 208-334-3233 to check a license or file a complaint. Licensing decisions there rest with the State Board of Morticians, whose members include a public member as well as licensed morticians, and its page links to the process for filing a complaint against a licensee.
cremation-costs-mississippi.html: The licensing office for cremation providers in Mississippi

The licensing office for cremation providers in Mississippi is the Mississippi State Board of Funeral Service; its number is 601-932-1973. The board has its office at 3010 Lakeland Cove, Suite W, in Flowood, and its fax number is 601-932-1901.
cremation-costs-vermont.html: In short, Vermont sets a 24-hour minimum before cremation

In short, Vermont sets a 24-hour minimum before cremation, and the crematory also needs the death certificate, a cremation permit and a signed authorization from the next of kin or designated agent. Vermont has no separate funeral board: the Office of Professional Regulation in Montpelier licenses funeral service with help from appointed advisors, and it handles complaints and discipline. For the exact Vermont citation, the funeral-director question and who takes complaints, see the cremation rules and help section lower on this page.
cremation-costs-arizona.html: Yes. An Arizona family can hold a viewing or service before cremation

Yes. An Arizona family can hold a viewing or service before cremation, and many providers rent a casket for it. Plan the date around the law: Arizona has no waiting period before cremation. The authorizing agent must give prior written consent and the medical examiner reviews the death certificate (A.R.S. § 32-1365.02). The authorizing agent is chosen by the priority order in A.R.S. § 36-831. When several people share the same rank, any one of them may sign unless another objects, and then a majority of those reasonably available decides; if no one is willing or able to pay, the county public fiduciary may order the cremation (A.R.S. § 32-1365.02).
cremation-costs-oregon.html: Crematories and the funeral homes that sell cremation in Oregon

Crematories and the funeral homes that sell cremation in Oregon answer to the Oregon Mortuary and Cemetery Board (971-673-1500). The board has eleven volunteer members appointed by the Governor, seven from the death care industry and four from the public, and it pays its way through licensing, examination and death record filing fees.
cremation-costs-texas.html: The licensing office for cremation providers in Texas

The licensing office for cremation providers in Texas is the Texas Funeral Service Commission; its number is 512-936-2474. The commission also regulates certain human anatomical donation programs, including willed body programs, so a question about donating a body to science goes to the same agency.
cremation-costs-louisiana.html: The licensing office for cremation providers in Louisiana

The licensing office for cremation providers in Louisiana is the Louisiana State Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors; its number is 504-838-5109. The board, formed in 1914 under La. R.S. 37:831, licenses crematory authorities and retort operators as well as funeral homes; its count on September 16, 2026 was 48 crematory authorities and 427 funeral establishments.
cremation-costs-north-carolina.html: What the law says about timing

What the law says about timing: North Carolina bars cremation within 24 hours after death, and a medical examiner must certify that no further examination is needed (N.C.G.S. 90-210.129, 130A-388). The same statute gives relatives and their invitees access to the crematory area, subject to the crematory's safety rules, and it requires remains to be kept at 40 degrees Fahrenheit or colder unless the cremation will begin within 24 hours of the crematory taking custody.
burial-costs-new-mexico.html: For New Mexico veterans, the plot and marker

For New Mexico veterans, the plot and marker in a national cemetery are free, which can remove thousands from a burial bill. In New Mexico, VA national cemeteries accepting burials: Fort Bayard National Cemetery (505-988-6400); Santa Fe National Cemetery (505-988-6400); state veterans cemeteries: Angel Fire State Veterans Cemetery (505-225-4341); Fort Stanton State Veterans Cemetery (505-205-6707); Gallup State Veterans Cemetery (575-921-3494) (source: VA National Cemetery Administration). The New Mexico Department of Veterans Services, which runs these cemeteries, also operates a fourth, Taos State Veterans Cemetery in Ranchos de Taos (505-470-3065), and lists its own numbers for Fort Stanton (505-383-4381) and Gallup (505-905-9770).
burial-costs-utah.html: For Utah veterans, the plot and marker

For Utah veterans, the plot and marker in a national cemetery are free, which can remove thousands from a burial bill. In Utah, VA national cemeteries accepting burials: Southern Utah National Cemetery (435-267-2710); state veterans cemetery: Utah Veterans Cemetery and Memorial Park (801-254-9036) (source: VA National Cemetery Administration). Southern Utah National Cemetery is in Cedar City, and the state-run Utah Veterans Cemetery and Memorial Park, in Bluffdale, is the closer option for families around Salt Lake City. The Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs reports VA grants of more than $16.5 million to add 1,400 columbarium niches at Bluffdale and to establish a new state veterans cemetery in Washington Terrace.
burial-costs-wyoming.html: Eligible Wyoming veterans get a grave

Eligible Wyoming veterans get a grave, opening and closing, a liner and a headstone at no cost in a national cemetery. In Wyoming, VA national cemeteries accepting burials: Cheyenne National Cemetery (307-778-7316); state veterans cemetery: Oregon Trail State Veterans Cemetery (307-235-6673) (source: VA National Cemetery Administration). Cheyenne National Cemetery is in the state's southeast corner, and the Oregon Trail State Veterans Cemetery is in Evansville, next to Casper. The Wyoming Veterans Commission was founded in 1981 to receive the federal funding that established the Evansville cemetery, and it still oversees it.
burial-costs-south-dakota.html: Eligible South Dakota veterans get a grave

Eligible South Dakota veterans get a grave, opening and closing, a liner and a headstone at no cost in a national cemetery. In South Dakota, VA national cemeteries accepting burials: Black Hills National Cemetery (605-347-3830); state and tribal veterans cemeteries: South Dakota Veterans Cemetery (605-277-8094); Akicita Owicahe Lakota Freedom Veterans Cemetery (tribal, 605-455-1497); Sicangu Akicita Owicahe Veterans Cemetery (tribal, 605-259-3044); Sisseton-Wahpeton Oyate Veterans Cemetery (tribal, 605-698-3388) (source: VA National Cemetery Administration). The Sicangu Akicita Owicahe Veterans Cemetery number comes from the tribe's office directory. The South Dakota Veterans Cemetery was dedicated on Memorial Day 2021 and held its first burials on June 4 that year; to arrange one, the family gives the cemetery the DD214 or enough service details for it to confirm eligibility.
burial-costs-texas.html: A Texas veteran's grave in a national cemetery

A Texas veteran's grave in a national cemetery costs the family nothing for the plot, opening and closing, or marker. In Texas, VA national cemeteries accepting burials: Dallas-Fort Worth National Cemetery (214-467-3374); Fort Bliss National Cemetery (915-564-0201); Fort Sam Houston National Cemetery (210-820-3891); Houston National Cemetery (281-447-8686); San Antonio National Cemetery (210-820-3891, cremated remains only); state veterans cemeteries: Central Texas State Veterans Cemetery in Killeen (254-616-1770); Coastal Bend State Veterans Cemetery in Corpus Christi (361-248-4830); Rio Grande Valley State Veterans Cemetery in Mission (956-583-7227); Texas State Veterans Cemetery in Abilene (325-673-4446); West Texas State Veterans Cemetery in Lubbock (806-392-9927) (source: VA National Cemetery Administration). All five state cemeteries are maintained by the Texas Veterans Land Board at the General Land Office.
burial-costs-north-carolina.html: For a license check or complaint about a funeral home arranging a burial in North Carolina

For a license check or complaint about a funeral home arranging a burial in North Carolina, call the North Carolina Board of Funeral Service at 919-733-9380; North Carolina cemeteries can have a separate regulator. For most cemeteries that regulator is the N.C. Cemetery Commission, which supervises cemeteries, their sales organizations and brokers, and preneed cemetery salespeople under Chapter 65, Article 9; cemeteries run by churches or government agencies fall outside that law.
burial-costs-vermont.html: For a license check or complaint about a funeral home arranging a burial in Vermont

For a license check or complaint about a funeral home arranging a burial in Vermont, call the Vermont Office of Professional Regulation at 802-828-1188; Vermont cemeteries can have a separate regulator. Vermont cemetery law sits in Title 18, Chapter 121. Under 18 V.S.A. § 5313, a cemetery's record of where remains are permanently placed must be open to the public at all reasonable times, and § 5323 lets a natural burial ground locate graves by mapping, surveying or GPS instead of a standard plat.
burial-costs-wisconsin.html: The Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services

The Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (608-266-2112) licenses the funeral homes that arrange burials in Wisconsin. It can also tell you which Wisconsin office handles cemetery complaints. Cemeteries themselves come under the Cemetery Board housed at DSPS, whose six members, four representing licensed cemetery authorities and two from the public, are appointed by the Governor for four-year terms.
